note: Failure modes an AI feature PRD can have. Each is backed by verbatim guest quotes; verify.py checks every quote against the transcript.

modes.name: Vibes-only quality bar
modes.check: The PRD defines quality only through demos, dogfooding or 'it looks good', with no repeatable measurement.
modes.pass_if: It names a repeatable check of output quality (a test set, a rubric, or a scored sample) that anyone on the team can rerun.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: Your vibe checks are very important, but they don't scale because they involve you, the human.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: once your product gets into production, more people start using it, you have more subject matter experts and engineers at your company that are actually contributing to its quality, then the vibe check version of an eval stops scaling.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: I've never seen somebody make it through multiple iterations of their product without any evals.

modes.name: Success criteria aren't measurable
modes.check: The requirements describe the AI behaviour in qualitative terms that an engineer cannot score.
modes.pass_if: Requirements include example inputs with expected behaviour, or criteria an engineer could score pass/fail.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: I think the modern PRD is an eval.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: an eval is the best way to communicate what your product should be doing

quotes.speaker: Aman Khan
quotes.quote: what if evals were your requirements instead of your AI product?

modes.name: Generic metrics instead of product-specific ones
modes.check: The eval plan leans on off-the-shelf scores (hallucination score, toxicity, BLEU, public benchmarks) rather than failures specific to this product.
modes.pass_if: Metrics are tied to concrete ways this product's output goes wrong for its users.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: the first thing to know about evals where people go off the rails is do not reach for generic metrics.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: there's a really big difference between foundation model benchmarks.

modes.name: Failure modes guessed, not observed
modes.check: The listed risks are brainstormed; there is no plan to read real outputs or traces and categorise what actually goes wrong.
modes.pass_if: It plans error analysis: reviewing a sample of real or realistic outputs and grouping the failures before choosing evals.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: you should be grounding it in things that are going wrong or the things that will probably go wrong.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: I keep looking at data and I just keep adding to my existing failure modes.

quotes.speaker: Teresa Torres
quotes.quote: for errors that are kind of persistent, I'm going to write an eval.

modes.name: LLM judge nobody checked
modes.check: The plan uses an LLM to grade outputs but never compares the judge with human labels.
modes.pass_if: The judge is measured against human-labelled examples, with an agreement target, before its scores are trusted.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: 80% of people who are using LLM as a judge are just writing a prompt and just praying that is doing the right thing.

quotes.speaker: Aman Khan
quotes.quote: I don't see too many people actually, when they talk about evals saying that you need to check the work of the LLM as a judge

modes.name: Fuzzy rubric
modes.check: Quality is graded on 1-to-5 or 1-to-10 scales, or with criteria too vague for two people to agree on.
modes.pass_if: Each criterion is binary (pass or fail) and specific enough that two reviewers would label the same output the same way.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: we say limit yourself to binary, because that is what the LLM can do very well.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: In our course, we define that as a rubric of binary criteria.

modes.name: Evals with no headroom
modes.check: The launch bar is near-perfect scores on a test set that is easy for today's model, so the evals cannot show progress or regressions.
modes.pass_if: The test set includes hard cases the current system fails, and the plan expects some evals to fail.

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: if you're getting 100% accuracy in your evals, it's likely your evals are worthless because they are providing you with no signal.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: one of the most important things is to have evals that fail.

modes.name: Offline only, no production loop
modes.check: Evals run before launch only; nothing samples live traffic or user feedback after launch.
modes.pass_if: It plans online checks: sampling production traces, user feedback signals, or regular re-scoring after launch.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: let's ship it into prod and see if they actually like it with an online eval.

quotes.speaker: Shreya Shankar
quotes.quote: Every week or so, I'll sample some of my traces, run my LLM-powered evaluators on them, and then kind of just look at the score, see if anything's off or whatnot.

modes.name: Cost and latency left out
modes.check: The PRD picks a model without budgets for cost per task or response time, or without testing whether a cheaper model is good enough.
modes.pass_if: It states cost and latency targets (ideally p95, not averages) and compares at least one cheaper model on the same eval.

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: They can let you understand whether a cheaper model can also go ahead and perform at a similar kind of level or not.

quotes.speaker: Ankit Shukla
quotes.quote: we will have the latency so p50 p95 p99 means that whenever we do averaging averaging is not going to give you the right kind of results

quotes.speaker: Hamel Husain
quotes.quote: evals are not free.

modes.name: Agent judged only on its final answer
modes.check: A multi-step agent is evaluated like a chatbot: one prompt in, one answer out, with no look at the steps or tool calls.
modes.pass_if: The plan evaluates whole tasks and inspects intermediate steps or tool calls where failures happen.

quotes.speaker: Daniel McKinnon
quotes.quote: this is a totally new paradigm of writing evals because you're no longer thinking about QA, you're thinking about tasks.

quotes.speaker: Ankur Goyal
quotes.quote: I set it up to evaluate every step. Maybe you only want to evaluate the last step
